title: Panel content sits twelve points from each edge, and indents mean a subsection
goal: The rows in Appearance are pushed in from the panel's left edge by more than the panel's own margin, so the section's content does not line up with its heading or with the sections above and below. Everything inside a panel section should sit twelve points from each edge. An indent should mean one thing only: this is a subsection folded under something above it. Nothing should be indented merely to make room for a control that some rows have and others do not.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-08 with a marked up screenshot asking for twelve points at each edge. Two separate causes, and both need fixing or the rows will still not line up. First, the shared value is wrong: EditorChromeLayout.panelEdgeInset (Sources/PhotonzCore/EditorChromeLayout.swift line 158) is 14, and every inspector applies it, so the outer margin is 14 rather than 12; note panelEdgeCenterInset at line 182 is derived from it, so changing it moves that too and the right hand icon alignment must be rechecked. Second, the extra indent the user is pointing at is inside the rows: PartsInspector.swift line 61 adds a leading pad of ColorPartLayout.nameLeading, which is the switch column width plus the gap (ColorStylePanel.swift line 254), so a row without a leading control is pushed in by the width of one that has. That is the indent to remove, replacing it with a proper column so a row with a control and a row without still begin at the same place. Coordinate with an-effect-row-reads-like-a-small-pane-with-a-che, which replaces the leading tick with a chevron and moves the switch to the right; if that lands first the leading column changes and this task should follow its shape rather than restore the old one.
acceptance: Every row in every panel section starts twelve points from the panel's left edge and ends twelve points from its right edge, measured in a render with the numbers in the audit
Rows that carry a leading control and rows that do not both start at that same left edge, so a section reads as one column rather than two
The only thing that shifts content further in is being a subsection folded under a heading, and the audit names anywhere that still indents for another reason
The measurement is one shared value, so a section added later cannot pick its own
Appearance, Effects, Position and Size, and every other section agree, not only the one reported
Nothing overlaps or clips at a narrow panel width
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a ruler over two sections before and after, anything rough filed as a follow-up
